CHAPTER IV OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 5
(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in providing Protection to Women and Children.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. implementing the obligations of Protection of Women and Children based on laws and regulations; b. establishing policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children; c. completing facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; .,---", d. allocating budget in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and e. fostering and supervising the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
Article 6 (1) The community has the obligation and responsibility in providing Protection to Women and Children.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented in the form of; a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. providing Protection to victims; c. providing emergency assistance; d. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities; and e. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

CHAPTER X COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 17 (1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children, the community may: a. form family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community; b. conduct independent socialization of the rights of Women and Children; c. provide first aid to victims; and d. report to the competent authority if violence against Women and Children occurs in the environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector and mass media.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabalong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Tabalong. 4. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tabalong Regency. 6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tabalong Regency. 7. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 8. Gender-based violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance of power in the relations between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women and children either physically, sexually and/or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere. 9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 10. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 11. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including the fetus in the womb. 12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence. 13. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an Integrated Activity Center that provides services for women and children victims of violence in Tabalong Regency free of charge covering information services, psychological consultation, legal and religious, assistance and advocacy as well as health services and safe houses with referrals.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 4 Every Woman and Child has the right: a. to have their dignity and worth as human beings respected; b. to obtain protection from family, community, Regional Government and/or other parties either temporarily or based on the determination of a protection order from the court; c. to restoration of physical, psychological and sexual health in accordance with the suffering experienced by the victim; d. to special handling related to the confidentiality of the victim; e. to assistance by social workers and legal aid at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; f. to spiritual guidance services; and g. to determine their own decisions.

CHAPTER VI MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 11
(1) To guarantee synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence in the Region.
(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of OPD implementing policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
(4) Monitoring is conducted starting from planning up to policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the current year.
Article 12
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children is conducted at the end of every fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The Protection of Women and Children is implemented based on the principles of: a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; e. legal certainty; and f. legal protection.
Article 3 The Protection of Women and Children aims to: a. prevent all forms of violence against Women and Children; b. protect women and children; and c. provide services to Women and Children victims of violence.

CHAPTER INSTITUTIONAL

(1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children in the Region, the Regent may establish P2TP2A.

(2) The establishment and development of P2TP2A shall be adjusted to the development of priority needs, and the financial capacity of the Region as well as the institutional and personnel capacity available in the Region.

(3) P2TP2A established by the Regional Government shall have at least 4 (four) counselors.

(4) Counselors as referred to in paragraph (3) include:
a. counselor in the field of law; b. counselor in the field of health; c. counselor in the field of psychology; and d. counselor in the field of religion.

Article 7 Article 8 

(1) Forms of services implemented at P2TP2A include:
a. legal consultation; b. assistance for victims; c. psychological consultation; d. medical service referral; e. safe house services with referral; f. home visit; and g. counseling.

(2) P2TP2A working partners include:
a. Health Office; b. Education Office; c. Social Office; d. RSUD; e. Puskesmas; f. Population and Civil Registration Office; g. PPA Unit (Polres and Polsek) h. TPPKK; i. Ministry of Religion; j. KUA; and k. Religious Court.

Article 9 

(1) The handling procedure at P2TP2A includes:
a. case reception; b. registration; c. case assessment; d. intervention planning; e. intervention agreement; f. intervention implementation; g. case recording; and h. termination.

a. legal services; b. medical services; c. psychological services; d. spiritual services; and e. safe house services.

CHAPTER VII REPORTING
Article 13
(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing reports on the implementation of P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children in the Region.
(2) Reporting on implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually or when necessary and submitted to the Provincial Government.
(3) The form of report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

In providing Protection to Women and Children, P2TP2A is obligated to: a. provide services as quickly as possible and free of charge to victims; b. organize protection and fulfillment of victims' rights to Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance; c. cooperate with certain institutions in providing translators and volunteer assistants needed for victims; d. provide convenience, comfort and safety for victims; and e. maintain the confidentiality of victims.

1.5.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the definition of “kekerasan berbasis gender” (Pasal 1 angka 8) covers suffering “baik secara fisik, seksual dan/ atau psikologis” plus threats, coercion, or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, in private/domestic and public spheres. Nowhere does it mention economic violence (kekerasan ekonomi), economic exploitation, deprivation of financial resources, neglect of economic needs, or similar. Other provisions (Pasal 4, 5, 6, 8–10) discuss protection, services, rehabilitation, reporting, and obligations, but still do not define or include economic violence. Therefore a ‘No’ is consistent with the source text; the golden ‘Yes’ appears incorrect.

1.8.rationale: The judge treated the ‘Mengingat’/legal-basis list (which includes UU No. 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang) as proof that trafficking is within the policy’s substantive scope. However, in the original Indonesian regulation, the operative provisions defining violence and services (notably Pasal 1 angka 8 on gender-based violence: physical/sexual/psychological + threats/coercion/deprivation of liberty) do not explicitly mention trafficking/perdagangan orang, nor do later chapters set out trafficking-specific measures. Citing a referenced statute in the preamble is not the same as the regulation explicitly covering trafficking as a form of violence for this indicator. So the evidence available supports ‘No’; the judge over-inferred from the legal-basis citation.

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

4.1.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Pasal 3 states a general aim to “mencegah segala bentuk kekerasan,” and Pasal 17(1)(b) says the community may “melakukan sosialisasi hak Perempuan dan Anak secara mandiri.” This is framed as optional community participation (“masyarakat dapat”), not a government-led prevention program, mandated public education campaign, or structured information/education intervention on VAW. The judge treated a general prevention aim plus optional community ‘sosialisasi’ as sufficient to mark the indicator ‘Yes.’ Given the source text, the golden ‘No’ is plausible and the judge’s reasoning is too lenient.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 4 Every Woman and Child has the right: a. to have their dignity and worth as human beings respected; b. to obtain protection from family, community, Regional Government and/or other parties either temporarily or based on the determination of a protection order from the court; c. to restoration of physical, psychological and sexual health in accordance with the suffering experienced by the victim; d. to special handling related to the confidentiality of the victim; e. to assistance by social workers and legal aid at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; f. to spiritual guidance services; and g. to determine their own decisions.

CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The Protection of Women and Children is implemented based on the principles of: a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; e. legal certainty; and f. legal protection.
Article 3 The Protection of Women and Children aims to: a. prevent all forms of violence against Women and Children; b. protect women and children; and c. provide services to Women and Children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VI MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 11
(1) To guarantee synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence in the Region.
(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of OPD implementing policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
(4) Monitoring is conducted starting from planning up to policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the current year.
Article 12
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children is conducted at the end of every fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IV OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 5
(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in providing Protection to Women and Children.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. implementing the obligations of Protection of Women and Children based on laws and regulations; b. establishing policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children; c. completing facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; .,---", d. allocating budget in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and e. fostering and supervising the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
Article 6 (1) The community has the obligation and responsibility in providing Protection to Women and Children.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented in the form of; a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. providing Protection to victims; c. providing emergency assistance; d. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities; and e. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

Article 10
In providing Protection to Women and Children, P2TP2A is obligated to: a. provide services as quickly as possible and free of charge to victims; b. organize protection and fulfillment of victims' rights to Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance; c. cooperate with certain institutions in providing translators and volunteer assistants needed for victims; d. provide convenience, comfort and safety for victims; and e. maintain the confidentiality of victims.

BAB XI CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 18 This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.
So that everyone may know of it, orders the Promulgation of this Regional Regulation by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Tabalong Regency.
Enacted in Tanjung on the date of 15 May 2017, REGENT OF TABALONG, :! ~

CHAPTER INSTITUTIONAL

(1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children in the Region, the Regent may establish P2TP2A.

(2) The establishment and development of P2TP2A shall be adjusted to the development of priority needs, and the financial capacity of the Region as well as the institutional and personnel capacity available in the Region.

(3) P2TP2A established by the Regional Government shall have at least 4 (four) counselors.

(4) Counselors as referred to in paragraph (3) include:
a. counselor in the field of law; b. counselor in the field of health; c. counselor in the field of psychology; and d. counselor in the field of religion.

Article 7 Article 8 

(1) Forms of services implemented at P2TP2A include:
a. legal consultation; b. assistance for victims; c. psychological consultation; d. medical service referral; e. safe house services with referral; f. home visit; and g. counseling.

(2) P2TP2A working partners include:
a. Health Office; b. Education Office; c. Social Office; d. RSUD; e. Puskesmas; f. Population and Civil Registration Office; g. PPA Unit (Polres and Polsek) h. TPPKK; i. Ministry of Religion; j. KUA; and k. Religious Court.

Article 9 

(1) The handling procedure at P2TP2A includes:
a. case reception; b. registration; c. case assessment; d. intervention planning; e. intervention agreement; f. intervention implementation; g. case recording; and h. termination.

(2) The handling procedure at P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d includes:
a. legal services; b. medical services; c. psychological services; d. spiritual services; and e. safe house services.

CHAPTER X COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 17 (1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children, the community may: a. form family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community; b. conduct independent socialization of the rights of Women and Children; c. provide first aid to victims; and d. report to the competent authority if violence against Women and Children occurs in the environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector and mass media.

6.2.rationale: The judge again relied on the preamble’s reference to UU No. 21 Tahun 2007 on trafficking to conclude the policy addresses trafficking victims as a specific (intersectional) group. In the operative Indonesian provisions, victims are defined broadly as “perempuan dan anak yang mengalami kekerasan” (Pasal 1 angka 12), and services/rights are provided generally to victims of violence; there is no explicit identification of trafficking victims (korban perdagangan orang) as a targeted subgroup with tailored measures. Therefore the available evidence does not support ‘Yes’; the judge over-inferred from a legal-basis citation rather than substantive provisions.
